mainTopic: The reforms of יוחנן כהן גדול, and what was lost after the סנהדרין ended and the בית המקדש was destroyed, especially the ban on song
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why יוחנן כהן גדול canceled the declaration of tithes. מעשר ראשון was going to the כהנים instead of the לויים, and since the declaration opens with the לוי's tithe, none of it can be said. A ברייתא seems to show that most people were not tithing at all. The גמרא answers that he made two separate rules: canceling the declaration was for the careful חברים, and the דמאי decree was for produce bought from עמי הארץ. The גמרא then explains his other reforms: stopping the לויים' daily 'עורה', stopping the cutting or beating of calves before שחיטה, and stopping hammering on חול המועד. A new משנה lists what was lost over time: song at wine feasts when the סנהדרין ended, the אורים ותומים, the שמיר, men of faith, and the blessing in dew and fruit after the חורבן. The גמרא brings strong warnings against song, with limits on which singing is allowed, and רבי יוחנן's teaching that drinking wine with music brings five punishments to the world.

steps.title: The tithe was going to the כהנים instead of the לויים
steps.stepSummary: The end of the reason for canceling the declaration: the תורה says to give מעשר ראשון to the לויים, but we give it to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we give it to the priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation of why יוחנן כהן גדול canceled the declaration of tithes. The point is that מעשר ראשון was being given to the כהנים, not to the לויים as the תורה says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration includes the words 'I have done everything You commanded me.' Since עזרא had moved מעשר ראשון away from the לויים to the כהנים, the farmer did not give it the way the פסוק describes. That means he cannot honestly say those words.

phrases.english: And we give it to the priests.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the tithe: the תורה says to give it to the לויים, but we give it to the כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to 'why did he cancel the declaration?' that began before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The declaration was canceled because מעשר ראשון is being given to כהנים rather than לויים, so it is not given as the תורה commands.

steps.title: Why not declare the other tithes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if he cannot declare מעשר ראשון, he should still declare the other tithes he gave properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him at least declare the other tithes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason just given. Only מעשר ראשון was being given the wrong way, so why cancel the whole declaration instead of saying it for the other tithes?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says the problem is too narrow to justify such a broad result. One faulty tithe should not wipe out the declaration for tithes that were given correctly, such as מעשר שני and מעשר עני.

phrases.english: And let him declare on the other tithes!
phrases.notes: אַשְּׁאָר is a short way of saying עַל שְׁאָר, 'about the other.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the reason in step 1 is enough to cancel the whole declaration.
steps.kashyaTarget: The full cancellation of the declaration.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only מעשר ראשון was given wrongly, so the declaration should still be said for the other tithes.

steps.title: No declaration for first tithe means no declaration at all
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that a household that cannot declare מעשר ראשון cannot declare any of the other tithes either.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Any house that does not declare about first tithe can no longer declare about the other tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge. The declaration is all or nothing: if מעשר ראשון cannot be declared, none of the other tithes can be declared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration is not a separate statement for each tithe. It is one unit, so a flaw in the מעשר ראשון part blocks the whole thing. The reason for this rule comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא רבי שמעון בן לקיש
first tithe, which the תורה gives to the לוי

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל בַּיִת שֶׁאֵין מִתְוַדֶּה עַל מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: Any house that does not declare about first tithe —
phrases.notes: 'House' here means a household, the owner of the produce.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּב אֵין מִתְוַדֶּה עַל שְׁאָר מַעַשְׂרוֹת.
phrases.english: no longer declares about the other tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ כׇּל בַּיִת שֶׁאֵין מִתְוַדֶּה עַל מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each tithe could be declared on its own.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the מעשר ראשון declaration, no tithe can be declared.

steps.title: What is the reason for ריש לקיש's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why failing to declare מעשר ראשון should block declaring the other tithes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source or logic behind ריש לקיש's rule. This question sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש stated the rule without giving a reason. The גמרא wants to know why מעשר ראשון has the power to hold back the whole declaration.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a missing מעשר ראשון declaration blocks the declaration of the other tithes.

steps.title: The verse opens with the first tithe
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the פסוק of the declaration begins with the לוי's tithe, so without it the declaration cannot be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because the verse begins with it first.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the reason. The פסוק of the declaration mentions giving to the לוי first, so if that part cannot be said, the rest cannot be said either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration's text opens with 'and I also gave it to the לוי' (דברים 26:13). The opening part is the base of the declaration. Without the first part, the following parts have nothing to rest on.
steps.whatToRemember: The declaration of tithes is one unit that opens with מעשר ראשון. If you cannot say that part, you cannot say any of it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Since the verse opened with it first.
phrases.notes: דברים 26:13. The declaration starts with giving to the לוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי הוֹאִיל וּפָתַח בּוֹ הַכָּתוּב תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק begins the declaration with מעשר ראשון, so the rest depends on it.

steps.title: Were people even separating tithes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the discussion assumes people were separating tithes, but a ברייתא says יוחנן כהן גדול found that many did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that they were separating tithes. But it is taught: He also canceled the declaration and decreed about דמאי. That was because he sent messengers throughout the land of Israel and saw that people separated only תרומה גדולה. As for first tithe and second tithe, some tithed and some did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the assumption behind the whole discussion. Canceling the declaration only because of where the tithe was going suggests people were tithing. A ברייתא, however, shows that many people were not tithing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the problem was only that מעשר ראשון went to כהנים, then people must have been separating it. The ברייתא tells us people separated only תרומה גדולה, and only some separated מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני. That suggests the declaration was canceled because people were not tithing, not because of where the tithe went.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it taught (in a ברייתא)?
produce bought from an unlearned person that may not have been tithed
the main תרומה given to the כהן from the crop

steps.confusionAlert: 'He' in the ברייתא is יוחנן כהן גדול, the same person from the משנה. The question is about the reason for his decree, not about someone else.

phrases.english: By implication, they were actually separating?
But isn't it taught:
He too canceled the declaration,
and made a decree about demai.
Because he sent messengers throughout all the borders of Israel

phrases.aramaic: וְרָאָה שֶׁאֵין מַפְרִישִׁין אֶלָּא תְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה בִּלְבַד,
phrases.english: and saw that they separated only teruma gedola,
and first tithe and second tithe —
some of them tithed and some of them did not tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְלָל דְּאַפְרוֹשֵׁי הֲווֹ מַפְרְשִׁי וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the reason in step 1 and challenges the assumption hidden inside it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied assumption in step 1 that people were separating tithes in יוחנן כהן גדול's time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא reports that most people separated only תרומה גדולה and many skipped the tithes. That contradicts the idea that tithes were being separated and merely given to the wrong person.

steps.title: The warning: untithed produce carries a death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: יוחנן כהן גדול told the people that eating טבל, or produce missing תרומת מעשר, is a sin punished by death, just like eating produce missing תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: My sons, come and I will tell you. Just as תרומה גדולה involves a sin punishable by death, so too תרומת מעשר and טבל involve a sin punishable by death.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to describe how יוחנן כהן גדול responded to the problem he found. He warned the people that skipping the tithes is just as serious as skipping תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People were careful to separate תרומה גדולה because they knew that eating produce before it was taken off carries death by the hand of Heaven. יוחנן כהן גדול taught that eating produce without תרומת מעשר, or eating any untithed טבל, carries that same punishment. This continuation shows how serious the neglect of tithes was, which strengthens the challenge in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: a sin punished by death (from Heaven)
the tenth the לוי gives from his tithe to the כהן
produce from which the required gifts have not yet been taken

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: בָּנַי, בּוֹאוּ וְאוֹמַר לָכֶם:
phrases.english: He said to them: My sons, come and I will tell you:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁתְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה יֵשׁ בָּהּ עֲוֹן מִיתָה —
phrases.english: Just as teruma gedola has in it a sin punishable by death —

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר וְטֶבֶל יֵשׁ בָּהֶן עֲוֹן מִיתָה.
phrases.english: so too the teruma of the tithe and untithed produce have in them a sin punishable by death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם בָּנַי בּוֹאוּ וְאוֹמַר לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא used in the challenge of step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating produce missing תרומת מעשר, or any untithed טבל, carries death by the hand of Heaven, just as missing תרומה גדולה does.

steps.title: The decree for produce bought from an unlearned person
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: יוחנן כהן גדול ruled that a buyer from an עם הארץ must separate מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני. He takes תרומת מעשר out of the מעשר ראשון for a כהן and eats the מעשר שני in ירושלים. But he does not have to hand over מעשר ראשון or מעשר עני, because the one who wants it must prove he is owed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He arose and made a rule for them: Someone who buys produce from an עם הארץ must separate first tithe and second tithe from it. From the first tithe he separates תרומת מעשר and gives it to a כהן. The second tithe he takes up and eats in ירושלים. As for giving away the first tithe and the poor man's tithe, whoever wants to take from his fellow must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 6 finishes. It tells us the practical rule יוחנן כהן גדול made because many people were not tithing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some parts of tithes carry a serious prohibition: תרומת מעשר is forbidden on pain of death, and מעשר שני must be eaten in ירושלים. So those parts must be dealt with even when it is only a doubt. The parts that are just money owed to the לוי or the poor person stay with the buyer, because nobody can prove the seller did not already give them.

keyTerms.meaning: He set up a rule (a rabbinic enactment)
An unlearned person who is not careful about tithes
Second tithe, which is eaten by its owner in ירושלים
Whoever wants to take something from another person must bring proof

steps.confusionAlert: מעשר ראשון shows up twice. The buyer does separate it, so that he can take the תרומת מעשר out of it. But he does not have to give the rest of it to a לוי.

phrases.english: He arose and instituted a rule for them:
phrases.notes: 'He' is יוחנן כהן גדול from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: One who buys produce from an unlearned person

phrases.aramaic: מַפְרִישׁ מֵהֶן מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: separates from it first tithe and second tithe.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן — מַפְרִישׁ מִמֶּנָּה תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר
phrases.english: From the first tithe, he separates the tithe-teruma
and gives it to a priest,
and the second tithe, he goes up and eats it in Jerusalem.
But first tithe and the poor man's tithe:
whoever wants to take from his fellow must bring proof!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in Steps 6-7 by giving the practical decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce bought from an עם הארץ (דמאי) needs מעשר ראשון and שני separated. תרומת מעשר goes to a כהן and מעשר שני is eaten in ירושלים, but the monetary parts (giving מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני) need proof before anyone can claim them.

steps.title: Two separate rules for two separate groups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 6. יוחנן כהן גדול made two different rules: cancelling the וידוי applied to the careful חברים, and the דמאי decree applied to the עמי הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made two separate rules: he cancelled the declaration of the חברים, and he made a decree about the uncertain produce of the עמי הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from Step 6. The two rulings are about two different groups of people, so they do not contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion assumed people were tithing. That fits the חברים, who did tithe, and their וידוי was cancelled only because of the problem with מעשר ראשון. The ברייתא about people not tithing is about the עמי הארץ, and that is what led to the separate דמאי decree.

keyTerms.meaning: The declaration a person makes once he has finished giving out his tithes
People committed to being careful about tithes and purity
Produce that may or may not have been tithed

steps.whatToRemember: The cancelled וידוי was for the careful חברים. The דמאי decree was for produce from the עמי הארץ. Two rules, two groups, no contradiction.

phrases.english: He instituted two things:
he cancelled the declaration of the careful ones,

phrases.aramaic: וְגָזַר עַל דְּמַאי שֶׁל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: and he decreed about the uncertain produce of the unlearned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא is finished, the גמרא resolves the challenge it raised in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ruling applies to a different group of people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the cancelled וידוי and the report that people weren't tithing describe the same people, so the discussion contradicts itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The וידוי ruling concerns the חברים, who did tithe. The 'not tithing' report and the דמאי decree concern the עמי הארץ.

steps.title: What were the awakeners?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, that יוחנן כהן גדול cancelled the מעוררים, and asks what they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he also cancelled the 'awakeners.' What are 'awakeners'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new item in the משנה and asks for the meaning of an unclear word. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gives a name, 'awakeners,' without saying what they did. Before we can understand why the practice was stopped, we need to know what it was.

phrases.english: And he also cancelled the awakeners.
What are awakeners?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tithes topic and goes back to the משנה's list of his reforms.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term מעוררים in the משנה.

steps.title: The לויים who called on God to wake up
steps.stepSummary: רחבה explains: every day the לויים on the platform said 'Awake, why do You sleep, ה׳‎.' יוחנן כהן גדול objected that God never sleeps. That פסוק is only meant for times when Israel suffers while the nations are at ease.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבה said: Every day the לויים would stand on the platform and say, 'Awake, why do You sleep, ה׳?' He said to them: Does God sleep? Doesn't it already say, 'Behold, the Guardian of Israel does not slumber or sleep'? Rather, that פסוק is said about a time when Israel suffers and the nations of the world live in calm and peace.
steps.whatsHappening: רחבה answers the question: the 'awakeners' were the לויים who said this פסוק every day. He also explains why יוחנן כהן גדול stopped it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'wake up' to God every single day could sound as if God really sleeps, which goes against another פסוק. The פסוק 'Awake' is meant as a cry for special times of suffering, not a daily routine. So the daily recital was stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform in the מקדש where the לויים sang

phrases.english: Raḥava said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹמְדִים לְוִיִּם עַל דּוּכָן
phrases.english: Every single day, when the Levites would stand on the platform
and say, "Awake, why do You sleep, O Lord?"
phrases.notes: תהלים 44:24

phrases.english: he said to them:
phrases.notes: 'He' is יוחנן כהן גדול.

phrases.english: Is there sleep before the Omnipresent?
Hasn't it already been said:

phrases.aramaic: ״הִנֵּה לֹא יָנוּם וְלֹא יִישָׁן שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל״!
phrases.english: "Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps"!
phrases.notes: תהלים 121:4

phrases.english: Rather, at a time when Israel is in suffering
and the nations of the world are in calm and serenity,
about that it is said, "Awake, why do You sleep, O Lord?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מעוררים were the לויים who said 'עורה למה תישן ה׳' every day. The practice was stopped because it suggested God sleeps, when the פסוק is really meant for times of suffering.

steps.title: What were the strikers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, the נוקפים, and asks what they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he also cancelled the 'strikers.' What are 'strikers'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes on to the next practice listed in the משנה and asks what the word means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like with the מעוררים, the משנה gives only a name. The גמרא needs to define the practice first.

phrases.english: And the strikers.
What are "strikers"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 10, now for the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term נוקפים in the משנה.

steps.title: Cutting the calf between its horns
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, explains: they cut the calf between its horns so blood would drip into its eyes. יוחנן כהן גדול stopped this because it looked like they were giving the animal a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They would cut the calf between its horns so that blood would fall into its eyes. He came and cancelled it, because it looks like a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains who the 'strikers' were and gives the reason יוחנן כהן גדול stopped them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cut was made so the blood would blind the animal and make it easier to slaughter. But an animal with a מום cannot be brought as a קרבן. Even though this cut was not a real disqualifying blemish, it looked like one, so he stopped the practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish that can disqualify an animal from being a קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: Both practices were stopped because of how they looked: the daily 'Awake' sounded as if God sleeps, and the cut looked like a blemish on a קרבן.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They would cut the calf between its horns,
so that blood would fall into its eyes.
He came and cancelled it,
because it looks like a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12 and adds the reason the practice was cancelled.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The נוקפים cut the calf between its horns so that blood would blind it. The practice was stopped because it looked like giving the animal a מום.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives a second explanation of the נוקפים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the נוקפים beat the calf with sticks, the way idol worshippers did. יוחנן כהן גדול protested that they were feeding נבילות to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: the נוקפים were people who beat the calf with sticks, the same way it is done before עבודה זרה. יוחנן כהן גדול said to them: How long will you keep feeding נבילות to the מזבח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the question from Step 12, 'what were the נוקפים?' This time the source is a ברייתא, and it describes beating the animal with sticks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13 שמואל said they cut the calf between its horns. The ברייתא says instead that they hit it with sticks to stun it before שחיטה, copying the practice of idol worshippers. יוחנן כהן גדול's complaint uses a strong word, נבילות, and the next step will question that word.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
Animals that died without a kosher שחיטה

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
that they would beat it with sticks
phrases.notes: 'It' is the calf being brought as a קרבן, the same animal from Step 13.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁעוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: the way they do it before idols.
He said to them: Until when
will you feed unslaughtered carcasses to the altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than שמואל in Step 13 to the question of what the נוקפים were.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What were the נוקפים? (asked in Step 12)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They beat the calf with sticks before שחיטה, the way idol worshippers did, and יוחנן כהן גדול called the animals נבילות.

steps.title: How can a slaughtered animal be called a נבילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: these animals were properly slaughtered, so they are not נבילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: נבילות? But he slaughters them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the word יוחנן כהן גדול used. A נבילה is an animal that died without שחיטה, but these calves were slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beating an animal does not kill it; the calf was still given a proper שחיטה afterward. So the label נבילה does not fit, and the גמרא needs to find what he really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here (used to point out a contradiction)

phrases.english: Unslaughtered carcasses?!
But he slaughters them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the word נבילות in יוחנן כהן גדול's complaint from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word נבילות in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נבילה is an animal that died without שחיטה. These animals were properly slaughtered, so the word cannot be accurate.

steps.title: He really meant טריפות, because the brain covering may be pierced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he meant טריפות: the beating might pierce the membrane around the brain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant טריפות, since perhaps the membrane of the brain was pierced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 15 by correcting the word. He did not mean נבילות but טריפות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is an animal with a fatal injury; even a perfect שחיטה does not make it kosher. Hitting the head with sticks might puncture the covering of the brain, which makes the animal a טריפה. So the worry was real, even though the word נבילות was not exact.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a fatal injury, which are forbidden even after שחיטה
The membrane that covers the brain

phrases.english: Rather, tereifot —
perhaps the membrane of the brain was pierced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 by reading נבילות as טריפות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He said נבילות, as if the animals had died without שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant טריפות: the beating might pierce the brain's membrane, making the animal forbidden even after שחיטה.

steps.title: יוחנן כהן גדול puts rings in the ground
steps.stepSummary: To solve the problem, יוחנן כהן גדול set up rings fixed in the ground to hold the animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: He got up and set up rings in the ground for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by telling us יוחנן כהן גדול's practical fix. Instead of beating the animals, they could tie them to rings in the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for beating the calf was to keep it still for שחיטה. Rings in the ground hold the animal in place, so there is no need to hit it and no risk of making it a טריפה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of the נוקפים: שמואל says they cut the calf between the horns (it looks like a מום), and the ברייתא says they beat it with sticks (it might become a טריפה). יוחנן כהן גדול's fix was rings in the ground.

phrases.english: He arose and instituted for them
rings in the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from Step 14 with the practical solution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Instead of beating the animals, they were held in place by rings fixed in the ground, so there was no risk of טריפות.

steps.title: The hammer in ירושלים means on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that until his days the hammer struck in ירושלים, and explains that this means on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until his days a hammer would strike in ירושלים. This means on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and explains it in two words: the hammer banging was on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could sound as if all hammering in ירושלים was stopped. The גמרא makes clear that only hammering on חול המועד was stopped by יוחנן כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the middle days of a יום טוב

phrases.english: Until his days a hammer would
strike in Jerusalem.
On the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד יָמָיו הָיָה פַּטִּישׁ מַכֶּה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the נוקפים to the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When was the hammer striking in ירושלים that the משנה refers to?

steps.title: No need to ask about דמאי, as already explained
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that in his days nobody had to ask about דמאי, and says this was already explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: All his days a person did not need to ask about דמאי. This is as we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last item in the משנה about יוחנן כהן גדול and simply points back to the earlier explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא explained that יוחנן כהן גדול made a rule about דמאי for food bought from עמי הארץ. Because of that rule, nobody needed to ask whether produce was tithed, so nothing new needs to be added here.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from an עם הארץ that might not have been tithed

steps.whatToRemember: This finishes the list of reforms of יוחנן כהן גדול: the וידוי, the דמאי rule, the מעוררים, the נוקפים, and the hammer on חול המועד.

phrases.english: All his days a person did not
need to ask about doubtfully tithed produce.
As we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier explanation of his דמאי rule, the one mentioned in Step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Covers the last item of the משנה by pointing back to the earlier discussion of דמאי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did no one need to ask about דמאי in his days?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because of his דמאי rule, already explained earlier.

steps.title: New משנה: when the סנהדרין stopped, song at wine feasts stopped
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that once the סנהדרין stopped, singing at feasts where wine was drunk was stopped too, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: From when the סנהדרין stopped, song was stopped from the places of feasting, as it says: 'With song they shall not drink wine.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, continuing the list of things that stopped over time. It says that singing at wine feasts ended when the סנהדרין ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the list was about the reforms of יוחנן כהן גדול. Now the משנה lists losses that came with the end of the סנהדרין, starting with song at drinking parties. It brings a פסוק from ישעיהו as its source.

keyTerms.meaning: The great court of Torah judges

phrases.english: MISHNA:
From when the Sanhedrin ceased —
song was stopped from the places of feasts,
as it is stated: “With song they shall not drink wine, etc.”
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of יוחנן כהן גדול's reforms is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the סנהדרין stopped, singing at feasts where wine is drunk was stopped, based on the פסוק 'With song they shall not drink wine.'

steps.title: The אורים ותומים stopped when the early prophets died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list: once the early prophets died, the אורים ותומים no longer worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time the early prophets died, the אורים ותומים stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps adding to its list of things that stopped over time. This item is the אורים ותומים, which stopped when the early prophets died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list follows the order of history. Each loss is tied to a turning point, and here the turning point is the death of the early prophets.

keyTerms.meaning: The names on the כהן גדול's breastplate, used to get answers from ה׳

phrases.english: From the time the early prophets died —
the Urim VeTummim stopped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of things that stopped, which began with singing at wine feasts ending when the סנהדרין stopped.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אורים ותומים stopped with the death of the early prophets.

steps.title: What was lost when the בית המקדש was destroyed
steps.stepSummary: When the בית המקדש was destroyed, the שמיר, the נופת צופים and the אנשי אמנה all disappeared, with a פסוק as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time the בית המקדש was destroyed, the שמיר and the sweetness of the honeycomb stopped, and men of faith disappeared from the Jewish people. As the פסוק says: "Help, ה׳, for the pious man is finished."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three things that ended with the destruction of the בית המקדש. It brings a פסוק for the loss of the faithful people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the turning point is the חורבן. The losses include a physical item (the שמיר), a special sweetness (נופת צופים), and a kind of person (אנשי אמנה). The פסוק about the pious being finished supports the last one.

keyTerms.meaning: A tiny creature that could cut stone
Men of faith, people you can trust completely

phrases.english: From the time the Temple was destroyed —
the shamir and the sweetness of the honeycomb stopped,
and men of faith disappeared from Israel,
as it is said: "Help, Lord,
phrases.notes: תהילים 12:2

phrases.english: for the pious man is finished, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the list forward in history from the early prophets to the destruction of the בית המקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the חורבן, the שמיר, נופת צופים and אנשי אמנה came to an end.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's testimony: blessing left the world
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reports that רבי יהושע testified that since the חורבן every day has a curse, the dew does not bring blessing, and fruit lost its taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that רבי יהושע testified: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, there is no day without a curse. The dew has not come down for blessing, and the taste has been taken from fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a testimony about how the world changed after the חורבן. It names three losses: a daily curse, dew without blessing, and fruit without taste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the list was about holy items and special people. Here it moves to the natural world: even dew and fruit became weaker after the חורבן.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
Rabbi Yehoshua testified:
From the day the Temple was destroyed
there is no day that has no curse in it,
and the dew has not come down for blessing,
and the taste of fruit has been taken away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues describing what the חורבן caused, now in the natural world.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the חורבן, every day has a curse, dew brings no blessing, and fruit has lost its taste.

steps.title: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר add to the losses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי adds that fruit also lost its richness. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains that losing טהרה took away taste and smell, and not separating מעשרות took away the richness of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: The richness of fruit was also taken away. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: The loss of purity took away the taste and the smell, and the tithes took away the richness of the grain.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more תנאים add to the list. רבי יוסי adds one more loss, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives the reasons for these losses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says fruit lost its fat too, not only its taste. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר goes further and explains why: when people stopped keeping טהרה, taste and smell were lost, and when they stopped giving מעשרות properly, grain lost its richness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
the richness of fruit was also taken away.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: הַטׇּהֳרָה נָטְלָה אֶת הַטַּעַם וְאֶת הָרֵיחַ,
phrases.english: purity took away the taste and the smell,
phrases.notes: He means the loss of purity, because people no longer kept it.

phrases.english: the tithes took away the richness of the grain.
phrases.notes: He means tithes that people didn't separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף נִיטַּל שׁוֹמֶן הַפֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רבי יהושע's list of losses and begins giving reasons for them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit also lost its richness. Losing טהרה caused the loss of taste and smell, and neglecting מעשרות caused the loss of the grain's richness.

steps.title: The חכמים: immorality and witchcraft ruined everything
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that זנות and כשפים destroyed it all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: Immorality and witchcraft destroyed everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give their own reason for all these losses. They blame them on זנות and כשפים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר tied each loss to a specific מצוה that was neglected. The חכמים give one broad cause instead: these two sins wiped out all the blessing.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה tells the story of Jewish decline in stages, ending with the losses after the חורבן. The תנאים argue about the cause: specific מצוות that were neglected, or the sins of זנות and כשפים.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
immorality and witchcraft destroyed everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: הַזְּנוּת וְהַכְּשָׁפִים כִּילוּ אֶת הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, broader cause than רבי שמעון בן אלעזר did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זנות and כשפים are the cause of all the losses.

steps.title: How do we know the end of singing is tied to the סנהדרין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by asking how we know that the פסוק about not drinking wine with song refers to the time after the סנהדרין stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And how do we know that the פסוק was written about the time after the סנהדרין stopped?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It goes back to the first part of the משנה (step 20) and asks for the source that links the end of singing to the end of the סנהדרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיהו says that people will not drink wine with song, but it doesn't mention the סנהדרין. So the גמרא asks what tells us the two are connected. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
And from where do we know

phrases.english: GEMARA
And from where do we know that it was written about the time after the Sanhedrin stopped?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the פסוק from step 20, "With song they shall not drink wine" (ישעיהו 24:9).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה ends, the גמרא returns to the משנה's first clause (step 20) and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What shows that the פסוק about wine without song refers to the time after the סנהדרין stopped?

steps.title: רב הונא's source: the Elders and the young men stopped together
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers from איכה: the Elders left the gate and the young men stopped their music, at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: Because the פסוק says: "The Elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their music."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 26 with a פסוק in איכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "Elders at the gate" are the judges of the סנהדרין. The פסוק puts their stopping right next to the young men's music stopping. That shows the end of song is tied to the end of the סנהדרין.

keyTerms.meaning: The Elders at the gate (the judges)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Because the verse says:
"The Elders have ceased from the gate,
phrases.notes: איכה 5:14

phrases.english: the young men from their music."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in איכה puts the end of the Elders at the gate (the סנהדרין) together with the end of the young men's music.

steps.title: רב: an ear that hears song should be uprooted
steps.stepSummary: רב states strongly that an ear that listens to song deserves to be torn out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: An ear that hears song should be uprooted.
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of singing, the גמרא brings a sharp statement from רב against listening to music.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said singing stopped once the סנהדרין stopped. רב turns this into a strong warning: since the חורבן, listening to song is so wrong that the ear doing it deserves to be uprooted.
steps.confusionAlert: רב is not giving a real punishment. This is a strong way of saying how bad it is to listen to song after the חורבן.

phrases.english: Rav said:
An ear that hears song — should be uprooted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the theme of song ending and adds a strong statement against listening to music.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Listening to song after the חורבן is very severely condemned.

steps.title: רבא: song in the house brings destruction to the doorway
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that song in a house leads to destruction at its doorway, and brings a פסוק from צפניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Song in the house means destruction at the doorway, as it says: "A voice will sing in the window, destruction at the doorpost, for its cedar work is uncovered."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another warning about song. He says it brings destruction to the home, and he backs this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב spoke about the person who listens. רבא speaks about the home: singing inside leads to ruin at the door. The פסוק puts singing in the window right next to destruction at the doorpost.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with רב's statement, this is the background for later discussions about how far the ban on music after the חורבן goes.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Song in the house —
destruction at the doorway,
as it is said: "A voice shall sing in the window,
phrases.notes: צפניה 2:14

phrases.english: destruction at the doorpost,
for its cedar work is uncovered."
phrases.notes: עֵרָה, 'uncovered,' can also be read as עִירָהּ, 'its city,' so the ruin reaches the whole city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second statement against song, this time about the home, with a פסוק as support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Song in a house brings destruction to its doorway, as shown by the פסוק in צפניה.

steps.title: What does 'for its cedar work shall be laid bare' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the last words of רבא's פסוק mean: כי ארזה ערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'כי ארזה ערה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the hard last words of the פסוק that רבא just quoted. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא used the first part of the פסוק to show that song in a house brings ruin to its doorway. Now the גמרא wants to know how the closing words, about cedar, fit into that idea.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'for its cedar work shall be laid bare'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the end of the פסוק quoted in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the words כי ארזה ערה and how they connect to song.

steps.title: Even a house built with cedars is shaken
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says a cedar-built house is as strong as a city, so the פסוק must mean that even such a strong house will be shaken by song.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: A house interlaced with cedars is as strong as a city! So the פסוק must mean that even a house interlaced with cedars will become shaky.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק first points out that a house built with cedar beams is very strong. Then he explains the פסוק: even a house that strong will be shaken when there is song in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, it seems strange that a cedar house should fall, since it is as solid as a whole city. רבי יצחק turns that strangeness into the lesson: song is so harmful that even the strongest house is not safe.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
A house interlaced with cedars is like a city!
Rather: even a house interlaced with cedars
becomes shaky.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: בַּיִת הַמְסוּבָּךְ בַּאֲרָזִים עִיר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק means that song ruins even a very strong house built with cedars.

steps.title: Destruction starts at the doorway
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי learns from the פסוק that ruin begins at the threshold of a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Learn from this that when destruction starts, it starts at the threshold, as it says: 'Destruction at the threshold.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes a new lesson from the same פסוק: when a house begins to be destroyed, the destruction starts at its doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words חרב בסף, 'destruction at the threshold', tell us where ruin begins. רב אשי turns this detail into a general rule about how destruction comes into a home.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Learn from this that when destruction starts —
it starts at the threshold,
as it is stated: 'Destruction at the threshold.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק from צפניה that רבא quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes a further lesson from the פסוק discussed in steps 29-31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Destruction of a house begins at its doorway.

steps.title: A second source: the gate is struck by שאיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another פסוק showing that destruction begins at the gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is learned from here: 'And the gate is struck by שאיה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different פסוק as the source for רב אשי's lesson that ruin starts at the entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the gate is the first thing struck, which fits the idea that destruction comes in through the doorway. The word שאיה is read as the name of a destroyer, which leads into the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: ruin; here a destroying force that strikes the gate

phrases.english: And if you want, say it from here:
'And the gate is struck by שאיה.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another source for the lesson of step 32.
steps.raayaObject: That destruction begins at the entrance.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי saw the destroyer
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says he saw the שאיה himself, goring like an ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: I saw it myself, and it was goring like an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי's son tells us he personally saw this destroyer at work, smashing things like a goring ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a real-life report to the פסוק. It shows that שאיה was understood as an actual destructive force, not only a word for ruin.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
I saw it myself,
and it was goring like an ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 33 with an eyewitness report.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The destroyer שאיה is real and was seen goring like an ox.
steps.whatToRemember: Song with drinking can shake even a strong house, and destruction comes in through the doorway.

steps.title: Work songs are allowed, weavers' songs are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא allows the songs of boat-pullers and herders but forbids the songs of weavers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The singing of those who pull boats and those who lead cattle is permitted. The singing of weavers is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא draws a line between kinds of singing: some workers may sing, and others may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boat-pullers and herders sing to help them work in rhythm or guide the animals, so the song serves the work. Weavers sing just for pleasure, so their song falls under the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: those who pull boats with ropes

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The song of boat-pullers and of cattle herders is permitted.
That of weavers is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: זִמְרָא דְּנַגָּדֵי וּדְבַקָּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the danger of song to the practical rules of which song is allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Song that helps with work is permitted; song only for enjoyment is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical limit to the strong words against song: not every song falls under the ban.

steps.title: When song stopped, food became cheap
steps.stepSummary: After רב הונא stopped singing, prices dropped greatly; after רב חסדא took the ban lightly, food became scarce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא stopped singing, and a hundred ducks sold for a זוז and a hundred סאה of wheat for a זוז, and nobody wanted them. Then רב חסדא came and took the ban lightly, and people looked for one duck for a זוז and could not find it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing what happened when song was stopped and what happened when the ban was weakened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב הונא's ban there was so much plenty that cheap food went unsold. Once רב חסדא treated the ban lightly, the blessing left and even one duck could not be found at that price.

phrases.english: Rav Huna stopped singing,
phrases.notes: He banned all singing, not just the forbidden kind from step 35.

phrases.english: and a hundred ducks stood at a zuz,
and a hundred se'ah of wheat at a zuz,
and they were not wanted.
Rav Chisda came and took it lightly,
a duck was wanted for a zuz
and it could not be found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story about רב הונא, whose ruling appears in step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stopping song brought plenty; weakening the ban brought scarcity.

steps.title: Men and women singing together
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that men singing with women answering is immoral, and women singing with men answering is like fire in kindling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Men singing and women answering is immodest behavior. Women singing and men answering is like fire in kindling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף describes two kinds of singing where men and women answer each other, and calls both bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds are forbidden, but the second sounds worse. When women lead and men answer, the bad desire catches quickly, like fire in dry kindling.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Men sing and women answer — that is immodest behavior.
Women sing and men answer —
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, but the corrected wording leaves it out. The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: it is like fire in kindling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: זָמְרִי גַּבְרֵי וְעׇנְיָין נְשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another kind of forbidden singing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both kinds are forbidden; women leading and men answering is the more dangerous one.

steps.title: Why does it matter which is worse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two kinds, since both are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב יוסף bothered to say which kind is worse, since both are forbidden anyway. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both are forbidden, ranking them seems to make no practical difference. The גמרא wants to find out when the ranking would matter.

keyTerms.meaning: what practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What practical difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the ranking in step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical use of saying one kind of singing is worse than the other.

steps.title: To stop the worse one first
steps.stepSummary: The ranking tells us which kind to stop first when we cannot stop both.
steps.simpleTranslation: To stop this one before that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ranking matters for deciding which kind of singing to stop first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people cannot be made to stop all such singing, they should at least stop the worse kind, where women lead and men answer. So the ranking gives an order of what to fix first.

phrases.english: To stop this one before that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When you cannot stop both, stop the worse kind first.

steps.title: Drinking with four instruments brings five punishments
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that drinking wine with four kinds of music brings five punishments, and starts quoting a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Anyone who drinks with four kinds of music brings five punishments to the world, as it says: 'Woe to those who get up early in the morning to chase strong drink, who stay up late at night while wine inflames them. The harp and lyre, drum and flute, and wine are at their feasts, and they do not look at the work of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן teaches that drinking wine with music causes harm to the whole world, and starts bringing his proof from a פסוק. The explanation of the five punishments continues after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names four instruments together with wine: harp, lyre, drum and flute. That is the source for the 'four kinds of music'; the five punishments will be explained next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who drinks with four kinds of music
brings five punishments to the world,
as it is stated: 'Woe to those who rise early in the morning to chase strong drink,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:11–12

phrases.english: 'who stay up late at night while wine inflames them,'
'and the harp and lyre, drum and flute,'
'and wine are at their feasts,'
'and they do not look at the work of the Lord,'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הַשּׁוֹתֶה בְּאַרְבָּעָה מִינֵי זֶמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the theme of drinking wine with song and opens a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking wine with four kinds of music brings five punishments to the world.

steps.title: The five punishments read from the verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוקים after the wine-and-music פסוק as listing five punishments: exile, famine, the תורה being forgotten, a 'lowering' of הקדוש ברוך הוא, and a lowering of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is written right after it? 'Therefore My people go into exile for lack of knowledge,' which means they cause exile to the world. 'And their honored men are famished' means they bring famine to the world. 'And their multitude are parched with thirst' means they cause the תורה to be forgotten by those who learn it. 'And mankind is bowed down, and man is humbled' means they cause a lowering of 'the enemy of הקדוש ברוך הוא', which is a respectful way of saying הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself. The word 'man' here can only mean הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says, 'ה׳ is a man of war.' 'And the eyes of the lofty are humbled' means they cause the lowering of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes explaining his claim from step 40. He takes each phrase of the next פסוקים in ישעיהו and shows that it describes one of the five punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 40 only gave the number five and the sinful behavior. Now each punishment is tied to its own words in the פסוק. To show that 'man' (אִישׁ) means הקדוש ברוך הוא, he brings proof from שמות, where הקדוש ברוך הוא is called 'a man of war'.

keyTerms.meaning: Thirst; read here as thirst for תורה
Literally 'the enemy of הקדוש ברוך הוא'; a respectful way to refer to Him without saying He is lowered

steps.whatToRemember: The five punishments are: (1) exile, (2) famine, (3) the תורה being forgotten, (4) a 'lowering' of הקדוש ברוך הוא, (5) a lowering of ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: 'The enemy of הקדוש ברוך הוא' does NOT mean some real enemy. It is a polite way of talking about הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself, so that the גמרא does not have to say outright that He is lowered.

phrases.english: What is written after it?
"Therefore My people go into exile for lack of knowledge"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:13

phrases.english: meaning that they cause exile to the world;
"and their honored men are famished"
meaning that they bring famine to the world;
"and their multitude are parched with thirst"
meaning that they cause the Torah
to be forgotten by those who learn it.
phrases.notes: The 'thirst' is read as thirst for תורה, which is often compared to water.

phrases.english: "And mankind is bowed down, and man is humbled"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:15

phrases.english: meaning that they cause a lowering
to the "enemy" of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
phrases.notes: This is a respectful way of speaking about ה׳ Himself.

phrases.english: For "man" means nothing other than the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is said: "The Lord is a man of war."
phrases.notes: שמות 15:3

phrases.english: "And the eyes of the lofty are humbled"
meaning that they cause the lowering of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה כְּתִיב אַחֲרָיו: לָכֵן גָּלָה עַמִּי מִבְּלִי דָעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's statement from step 40 by listing and sourcing each of the five punishments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking wine with music causes exile, famine, the forgetting of תורה, a lowering of הקדוש ברוך הוא, and a lowering of ישראל.

steps.title: Opening one more verse after the five punishments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting another פסוק that comes after these, to show a further consequence.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is written after it? 'Therefore...'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to quote the next פסוק in ישעיהו, and the rest of it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five punishments are complete, but the גמרא keeps reading the same passage to bring one more result of this behavior. Only the opening word 'לכן' appears here. The explanation comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore; opens a פסוק that describes a consequence

phrases.english: And what is written after it? "Therefore..."
phrases.notes: The פסוק keeps going on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the five punishments, the גמרא continues to the next פסוק in the same passage of ישעיהו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up another פסוק describing a further consequence of drinking wine with music.
